# New renderings chosen in odyssey-098 (20.1–97)

Rows in the format of the House renderings table in `conventions.md`: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| κακὰ φρονέων (20.5, μνηστῆρσι κακὰ φρονέων ἐνὶ θυμῷ) | "evil thinking" | "meaning evil" | "plotting", "devising", "scheming"; follows the table's κακὰ φρονέουσα ἐνὶ θυμῷ (10.317) "evil thinking in her heart" / "meaning evil in her heart"; kept apart from δολοφρονέων "with guile in his mind" |
| ἀγαιομένου κακὰ ἔργα (20.16) | "he being indignant at the evil deeds" | "indignant at those evil deeds" | "enraged", "resenting", "angry at" (ἀγαίομαι is "be indignant"); kept apart from the ἀγάασθε "begrudge" of Calypso’s speech to the gods |
| στῆθος δὲ πλήξας κραδίην ἠνίπαπε μύθῳ (20.17, whole line) | "And his chest having struck, his heart he rebuked with a word:" | "Then he struck his chest and rebuked his heart in these words:" | "scolded", "reproached"; "rebuke" is kept for ἐνίπτω and νεικέω, as in the table's ὁμοκλή row |
| τέτλαθι δή, κραδίη (20.18) | "Endure now, heart" | "Endure, now, my heart" | "Bear up", "Be patient", "Hold on" (τλάω is "endure" throughout, as in πολύτλας) |
| καὶ κύντερον ἄλλο ποτ’ ἔτλης (20.18) | "even more dog-like another thing once you endured" | "You once endured something even more shameless than this" | "worse", "more savage"; follows the table's κύντερον "more dog-like" / "more shameless" |
| μένος ἄσχετος (of the Cyclops, 20.19; nominative beside the vocative μένος ἄσχετε in the table) | "unrestrained in fury" | "unrestrained in his fury" | "of irresistible might", "of unconquerable strength"; follows the table's μένος ἄσχετε |
| ἐτόλμας (20.20, imperfect of τολμάω) | "you bore it" | "you held out" | "you dared" (reserved for θαρσέω), "you endured" (the table gives ἐπιτολμάω "endured", but here it would hide the near-repetition ἔτλης / ἐτόλμας, which is kept visible only through the note) |
| ἐν πείσῃ μένε (20.23, of the heart) | "remained in obedience" | "stayed obedient" | "stayed under the rein", "held steady" (the rare noun πείση is "obedience", from πείθομαι) |
| ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα (20.24, 26, 28) | "here and there" | "this way and that" | "to and fro", "hither and thither"; already the shipped wording (e.g. in odyssey-025), listed so it is table-fixed |
| γαστήρ (20.25, a stuffed animal's stomach roasted on the fire) | "a paunch" | "a paunch" | "belly" (reserved for the plain γαστήρ of hunger), "sausage", "stomach"; the note says what a paunch is |
| σχεδόθεν δέ οἱ ἦλθεν Ἀθήνη / οὐρανόθεν καταβᾶσα (20.30–31) | "And near at hand came to him Athena, / from heaven having come down" | "Athena came close to him, descending from the sky" | "from Olympus"; οὐρανός is "heaven" in `l` and "sky" in `i`, as in the table's σιδήρεος οὐρανός (15.329) and the shipped οὐρανόθεν (odyssey-025, -029, -040); the shipped σχεδόθεν wording is kept |
| πάϊς (20.35, nominative, "a son") in οἶκος … γυνὴ … καὶ πάϊς | "a son" | "a son" | "child", "boy"; Odysseus's son is named Telemachus elsewhere, but here the word is a plain "son" |
| μερόπων ἀνθρώπων (20.49; meaning of μέροπες not known) | "speech-dividing men" | "men of articulate speech" (+ note: meaning not known; the ancient explanation "having divided speech", i.e. articulate, is followed; "mortal" is the other guess) | "mortal men" (silently picks the other guess; "mortal" is kept for βροτός and θνητός), "speech-endowed", "of human speech" |
| κτεῖναι μεμαῶτες Ἄρηϊ (20.50) | "eager to kill with Ares" | "eager to kill us in battle" | "eager for the kill", "bent on war"; Ἄρηϊ stands for war, as in the table's βροτολοιγὸς Ἄρης only as the god's name |
| ἴφια μῆλα (20.51) | "stout flocks" | "stout flocks" | follows the table's ἴφια μῆλα (11.108), listed because here it is joined to βόας "cattle" |
| ἀνίη … τὸ φυλάσσειν πάννυχον ἐγρήσσοντα (20.52–53) | "irksome also is the keeping watch all night awake" | "To keep watch all night, awake, is tiresome too" | "grievous", "wearisome" (reserved for κάματος); follows the table's ἀνίη "irksomeness" / "tiresome" |
| κακῶν ὑποδύσεαι (20.53) | "from under evils you will slip out" | "you will slip out from under your troubles" | "you will be rid of", "you will escape" (lose ὑπο- "from under"), "sink beneath" (the opposite sense) |
| ὕπνον ἐπὶ βλεφάροισιν ἔχευεν (20.54) | "sleep upon the eyelids she poured" | "poured sleep over his eyelids" | "cast sleep" (the verb is χέω, as in the shipped γλυκὺν ὕπνον ἔχευε "poured sweet sleep"; βάλε is "cast"), "closed his eyes" |
| εὖτε τὸν ὕπνος ἔμαρπτε, λύων μελεδήματα θυμοῦ, / λυσιμελής (20.56–57) | "When him sleep was seizing, loosing the cares of his heart, / limb-loosening" | "As sleep took hold of him, loosing the cares of his heart and slackening his limbs" | "sleep, the limb-looser" (makes λυσιμελής a noun), "relaxing", "slack-limbed"; μελεδήματα keeps "cares", as shipped |
| πυκινῶς ἀκαχήμενος ἦτορ (20.84) | "thickly grieved in heart" | "sorely grieved at heart" | "bitterly", "deeply", "closely"; follows the table's ἀκαχήμενος ἦτορ "grieved in heart" / "grieved at heart" |
| ἀψόρροος Ὠκεανός (20.65, ἀψορρόου Ὠκεανοῖο) | "back-flowing Oceanus" | "back-flowing Oceanus" | "ever-returning", "circling", "reverse-flowing"; built like the table's βαθύρροος Ὠκεανός "deep-flowing Oceanus" |
| ἠερόεντα κέλευθα (20.64) | "the misty paths" | "the misty paths" | "murky", "dark", "hazy" (ἠερόεις is built on ἀήρ "mist", as in ἠεροειδής); follows the table's ὑγρὰ κέλευθα "the watery ways" for κέλευθα, with "paths" in place of "ways" |
| εἶδος καὶ πινυτήν (20.71) | "beauty and discernment" | "beauty and discernment" | "prudence" (reserved for πεπνυμένος), "wisdom", "good sense"; πινυτή is the noun of the table's πινυτός "discerning" |
| μῆκος (20.71, a gift of Artemis) | "height" | "height" | "stature" (reserved for φυή), "tallness", "length" |
| ἔργα … κλυτὰ ἐργάζεσθαι (20.72) | "works … famous … to work" | "to work famous works" | "glorious deeds", "splendid crafts"; κλυτός keeps "famous" |
| τέλος θαλεροῖο γάμοιο (20.74) | "the fulfilment of blooming marriage" | "the fulfilment of a blooming marriage" | "the end of", "the completion of" (τέλος is also "end"), "lusty"; follows the table's θαλερὸς γάμος |
| μοῖράν τ’ ἀμμορίην τε (20.76) | "both the portion and the lack of portion" | "both the portion and the lack of portion" | "good and ill fortune" (explains rather than translates; the note gives it), "fate and fatelessness"; μοῖρα keeps the "portion" of μόρος |
| ἀνηρείψαντο (20.77) | "snatched away" | "carried off" | follows the shipped ἀνηρείψαντο "snatched away" / "carried off" |
| ἀϊστώσειαν (20.79) | "make vanish" | "make vanish" | "destroy", "blot out", "annihilate" (ἀϊστόω is "make unseen"), "make disappear" |
| ὀσσομένη (20.81) | "picturing" (Odysseus … picturing) | "with Odysseus before my eyes" | "seeing", "looking for", "foreseeing" (each picks one sense of ὄσσομαι) |
| ἀνεκτὸν ἔχει κακόν (20.83) | "even bearable holds the evil" | "is an evil one can even bear" | "tolerable", "endurable" (Latinate), "bearable" in `l` only |
| ἐπέσσευεν κακὰ δαίμων (20.87) | "against me … drove evil, some power" | "some power has driven … evil … upon me" | follows the shipped ἐπέσσευεν "drove" (odyssey-090), with δαίμων "some power" |
| παρέδραθεν εἴκελος αὐτῷ (20.88) | "slept beside me one like to him himself" | "someone lay beside me, the very likeness of him" | "a man like him", "his image" (the Greek does not say the figure was a man or a dream until ὄναρ in line 90) |
| ἐφάμην ὄναρ ἔμμεναι, ἀλλ’ ὕπαρ ἤδη (20.90) | "I did not say it was a dream, but now a waking sight" | "I did not suppose it was a dream, but already a waking sight" | "a vision", "reality", "the real thing"; follows the table's ὕπαρ / ὄναρ "waking sight" / "dream" |
| ὣς ἔφατ’, ἐν στήθεσσι καθαπτόμενος φίλον ἦτορ (20.22, whole line) | "So he spoke, in his breast accosting his dear heart;" | "So he spoke, addressing his dear heart in his breast." | "rebuking" (the rebuke is the line before), "speaking to his heart"; follows the table's καθαπτόμενος row |
| τῆς δ’ ἄρα κλαιούσης ὄπα σύνθετο δῖος Ὀδυσσεύς (20.92, whole line) | "And of her weeping the voice took in heavenly Odysseus;" | "And heavenly Odysseus heard the voice of her weeping;" | "noticed", "recognised" (the Greek does not say he knew whose it was until the next line); σύνθετο keeps "took in" in `l` |
| χεῖρας ἀνασχών (20.97) | "his hands raising" | "raising his hands" | follows the shipped χεῖρας ἀνασχών (odyssey-065, odyssey-084) |
